chapters.title: Audit log and compliance
intro: This chapter is for administrators and the people who handle data protection. It explains the audit log, which records sensitive actions in a way nobody can quietly change.
It also covers the **Compliance** page. There you set how long to keep data, place legal holds, handle customers' data requests and decide on support access.

sections.title: What the audit log records
intro: The audit log records sensitive actions in your workspace. You need the **View audit logs and verify integrity** permission to open it.
Every change and its log entry are saved together, so no change goes unrecorded.

list: Changes to roles, permissions and settings.
Exports, deletions, merges and entitlement overrides.
Keys and OAuth clients, AI actions and subscription changes.

blocks.p: Every few seconds, SupportDesk seals new entries into a chain. Each sealed entry carries a fingerprint of the entry before it. If anyone changes or removes an entry, the chain breaks, and **Verify chain** finds it.
New entries show **sealing** until they are sealed. When a retention policy removes old entries, the check starts from a recorded starting point.

sections.title: The Audit log page
sections.intro: Open it with **Administration** > **Audit log**. The newest entries come first.

blocks.caption: The **Audit log** page. The newest entry still shows **sealing**.
blocks.alt: Audit log page with Export CSV, Verify chain, the filter form and the list of entries

callouts: **Export CSV** saves the filtered entries as a spreadsheet file.
**Verify chain** checks that no entry was changed or removed.
The filters. **Apply** filters the list and **Clear** resets it.
One entry. **#** shows its place in the chain, or **sealing** while it is new.

blocks.p: The columns are **When**, **Actor**, **Action**, **Entity**, **Summary**, **IP** and **#**. Select **Load more** at the bottom to see older entries.

sections.title: Find audit entries
sections.intro: Filter the log to answer a question, such as who changed a role last week.
steps: Fill in one or more filters. See the table below.
To see more entries, select **Load more** at the bottom.
sections.result: The list shows only matching entries. If nothing matches, it says **No audit entries match**.

rows: One kind of action, such as `auth.login`.
The kind of record, such as **User** or **Tenant**.
The full identifier of one record. Copy it from another entry.
The first and last day to include.
The start of a network address, such as `10.0.`.

sections.title: Open an audit entry
sections.intro: Open an entry to see exactly what changed.
steps: In the audit log, select the entry.

steps.text: Read the facts and the **Changes** table.
steps.caption: The **Audit entry** panel for a sign-in, with what it recorded.
steps.alt: Audit entry panel with when, actor, action, entity, summary, client, sequence, hashes and the changes table

steps: Select the close button to return to the list.
sections.result: You see who did what, when, from where, and each field's value before and after.

rows: When it happened, who did it and what they did.
The record it affected, and a short description.
The network address and the browser or app used.
A reference shared by all entries from one action. Use it to find related entries.
The entry's place in the chain and its fingerprints.
Each field with its **Before** and **After** value.
Everything the entry stored, in full.

sections.title: Export the audit log
sections.intro: Export entries for an auditor or for your own records.
steps: Set the filters for the entries you need, and select **Apply**.
sections.result: Your browser saves a file named `audit-` followed by the date. It opens in Excel or any spreadsheet app.

blocks.note: One export holds up to 50,000 entries. Cells that a spreadsheet could run as formulas are made safe. The export itself is recorded in the audit log.

sections.title: Verify the audit chain
sections.intro: Check that no audit entry was changed or removed. Do it before an audit, or when you suspect tampering.
steps: Read the result at the top of the page.
sections.result: **Audit chain intact.** means the log is complete. The line below says how many entries were checked and how many still wait for sealing.

blocks.warning: If the result says **Audit chain broken!**, select **Open entry** to see the first bad entry. Tell your security team and your SupportDesk provider at once.

blocks.note: Each check is itself recorded in the audit log.

sections.title: The Compliance page
intro: Open it with **Administration** > **Compliance**. You need the **Retention, legal holds, data export and erasure** permission.
The page has four tabs: **Retention**, **Legal holds**, **Data requests** and **Support access**.

blocks.caption: The **Retention** tab with the demo workspace's three policies.
blocks.alt: Compliance page on the Retention tab with three policies and their actions

callouts: The four tabs of the **Compliance** page.
A policy: its name, its rule, its last run and whether it is **Active** or **Paused**.
**Dry run**, **Run now**, the edit button and the delete button.

sections.title: Retention data and actions
intro: A retention policy removes or hides data after a number of days. Each kind of data allows some actions and has a minimum age.
Records covered by an active legal hold are never archived, anonymised or deleted.

rows: Tickets closed more than the set number of days ago.
Raw e-mail, chat and social messages. The ticket conversation stays.
Old sealed audit entries. The chain stays checkable.
Records of AI calls and their results.

list: **Anonymize** keeps the numbers for reports, but removes the text. A ticket's subject becomes `[redacted]`. Its description, resolution, survey comment, AI summary and custom fields are cleared.
**Delete** removes the records, their search entries and unused files for good.
A run on the audit log removes only the oldest sealed entries, up to 10,000 a run.

sections.title: Create a retention policy
sections.intro: Create a policy to keep data only as long as you need it.
steps: Enter a **Name**, such as `Archive old closed tickets`.
In **Data**, choose the kind of data. The hint below explains it.
To run the policy on its own, keep **Run automatically every day** on.

steps.text: Read the blue box. It says how many records the policy would affect now.
steps.caption: A new policy that archives closed tickets after 730 days.
steps.alt: New retention policy panel with name, data, action, days, the automatic switch and the live count

sections.result: The app shows **Policy created**. The policy appears in the list.

blocks.note: Active policies run every six hours, in batches.

sections.title: Check a policy with a dry run
sections.intro: A dry run counts what a policy would affect now. It changes nothing.
steps: On the **Retention** tab, find the policy.

steps.caption: The result line under a policy after a dry run.
steps.alt: Retention policy list with a dry-run result line under the closed tickets policy

sections.result: A line under the policy shows how many records it would affect, and how many legal holds keep. It also shows the cut-off date.

sections.title: Run a retention policy now
sections.intro: Run a policy at once instead of waiting for the automatic run.
steps: On the **Retention** tab, select **Dry run** on the policy, and check the numbers.

steps.warning: A **Delete** policy removes records for good. Check the dry run first.

sections.result: The app shows **Retention run complete** with the number of records affected and kept by legal holds.

blocks.note: One run handles up to 1,000 records. Run it again for more. Every run is recorded in the audit log.

sections.title: Change, pause or delete a retention policy
sections.intro: Change a policy's rule, stop it from running on its own, or remove it.
steps: On the **Retention** tab, select the edit button on the policy's row.
In **Edit retention policy**, make your changes.
To pause the policy, turn off **Run automatically every day**.
To remove a policy, select the delete button on its row. In the dialog, select **Delete**.
sections.result: The app shows **Policy saved**. A paused policy shows **Paused** in the **Active** column.

sections.title: Legal holds
intro: A legal hold preserves records during a dispute, an audit or an investigation. A hold covers the tickets that match all the criteria you set.
Held tickets keep their messages, attachments and AI records. Retention skips them, and nobody can delete them. A hold also blocks erasure of the contacts involved.

blocks.caption: The **Legal holds** tab with one active hold.
blocks.alt: Legal holds tab with the Show released holds switch, the Place legal hold button and one active hold

callouts: **Show released holds** adds released holds to the list.
**Place legal hold** creates a new hold.

blocks.p: Each hold shows its name, reason and who placed it. **Covers** lists its criteria. **Tickets** counts the tickets it covers now. **Status** is **Active** or **Released**.

blocks.note: You cannot change a hold. To change one, place a new hold, and then release the old one.

sections.title: Place a legal hold
sections.intro: Place a hold as soon as you learn that records may be needed as evidence.
steps: Set at least one criterion: **Customer**, **Contact**, **Ticket numbers** or the **Created from** and **Created until** dates.

steps.text: For **Ticket numbers**, press [[Enter]] after each number.
steps.caption: The **Place legal hold** panel with a name filled in.
steps.alt: Place legal hold panel with name, reason, customer, contact, ticket numbers and created dates

sections.result: The app shows **Legal hold placed** with the number of tickets now preserved.

sections.title: Release a legal hold
sections.intro: Release a hold when the matter is closed.
sections.result: The app shows **Legal hold released**. The records follow the retention policies and erasure requests again.

blocks.tip: Turn on **Show released holds** to see past holds.

sections.title: Data-subject requests
intro: Customers can ask for a copy of their data, or ask you to erase it. Record such requests on the **Data requests** tab. Every step is recorded in the audit log.
A contact can have only one open request of each type.

blocks.caption: The **Data requests** tab before any request is recorded.
blocks.alt: Data requests tab with the Status filter and the New request button

callouts: **New request** records an export or an erasure request.

rows: An erasure request waits for an administrator's decision.
SupportDesk is building the export or erasing the data. The list refreshes on its own.
The export is ready, or the erasure is done.
An administrator rejected the erasure. The reason shows under the status.
Something went wrong. The error shows under the status.

sections.title: Export a contact's data
sections.intro: Give a customer a copy of the data you hold about them.
prerequisites: You have checked the person's identity.
steps: In **Contact**, search for and choose the person.

steps.text: In **Notes**, record how the request arrived and how you checked the person's identity.
steps.caption: A new export request with notes about the identity check.
steps.alt: New data-subject request panel with Export chosen, the contact search and notes

steps: When the status changes to **Completed**, select **Get link**.
Select **Download export**, and send the file to the customer securely.
sections.result: Your browser saves a zip file with the contact's profile, identities, consents, tickets, messages and attachments.

blocks.warning: The link works once and expires after 24 hours. SupportDesk removes the export after the download.

sections.title: Request erasure of a contact's data
sections.intro: Record a customer's request to be forgotten. The erasure waits for approval.
prerequisites: You have checked the person's identity.
steps: In **Notes**, record how the request arrived and how you checked the identity.
sections.result: The app shows **Erasure requested**. The request waits with the status **Awaiting approval**.

sections.title: Approve or reject an erasure
sections.intro: Decide on an erasure request after you check it.
prerequisites: Another administrator made the request. If someone else holds the compliance permission, you cannot approve your own request.
steps: To reject, select **Reject**. Enter a **Reason**, and select **Reject**.

steps.warning: **Approve erasure** asks for no confirmation. The erasure cannot be undone.

sections.result: The app shows **Erasure approved**. SupportDesk erases the contact in the background.

blocks.p: Erasure renames the contact to **Erased contact** and clears their personal details, identities, consents and portal access. Their messages become `[erased at the customer's request]`, and their uploads are deleted. Ticket statistics stay.

blocks.note: If a legal hold covers the contact, the row says **Blocked by a legal hold**. **Approve erasure** is then greyed out.

sections.title: Support access
intro: SupportDesk staff never sign in as your users. When they need to diagnose a problem, they ask for read-only access for a limited time.
During access, they see usage, configuration counts, failed jobs and recent audit entries. They never see tickets or customer data.

blocks.caption: The **Support access** tab with one pending request from the platform operator.
blocks.alt: Support access tab with a pending request and the Reject and Approve buttons highlighted

blocks.p: Each request shows who asked, when, for how many minutes and why. **Status** shows **Pending** until you decide. While access is active, the row shows when it ends.

sections.title: Approve, reject or revoke support access
sections.intro: Decide on a support access request, or end access early.
steps: Read the reason and the duration of the request.
To approve, select **Approve**. In the dialog, select **Approve**.
To end active access early, select **Revoke**.
sections.result: The app shows **Access approved**, **Request rejected** or **Access revoked**.

blocks.note: Every step is recorded in your audit log and in the platform's audit log. While your workspace is suspended, you cannot approve access.

troubleshooting.problem: **Entity id** shows an error when you select **Apply**.
troubleshooting.cause: The value is not a complete record identifier.
troubleshooting.fix: Copy the identifier from the **Entity** line of another entry, or clear the field.

troubleshooting.cause: Your plan does not include **Audit export**.
troubleshooting.fix: Change to a plan with **Audit export**. See the plan comparison on the **Subscription** page.

troubleshooting.cause: An audit entry was changed or removed outside SupportDesk.
troubleshooting.fix: Select **Open entry** to see the first bad entry. Tell your security team and your SupportDesk provider at once.

troubleshooting.problem: The app says a policy must keep data for at least a number of days.
troubleshooting.cause: **After (days)** is below the minimum for that kind of data.
troubleshooting.fix: Enter at least the minimum shown under **After (days)**.

troubleshooting.problem: **Approve erasure** is greyed out, and the row says **Blocked by a legal hold**.
troubleshooting.cause: An active legal hold covers the contact.
troubleshooting.fix: Wait until the matter is closed. Then release the hold and approve the request.

troubleshooting.problem: The app says another compliance administrator must approve the erasure.
troubleshooting.cause: You made the request yourself. A second person must approve it.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask another administrator with the compliance permission to approve it.

troubleshooting.problem: The export download link does not work.
troubleshooting.cause: The link works once and expires after 24 hours.
troubleshooting.fix: Record a new export request for the contact.

faq.q: Can SupportDesk staff read our tickets?
faq.a: No. With approved support access, they see only usage, configuration counts, failed jobs and recent audit entries. They never see tickets or customer data.

faq.q: Can I undo an erasure or a deletion?
faq.a: No. Erased and deleted data cannot be recovered. Use **Dry run** and check requests before you approve them.

faq.q: Does a legal hold stop agents from working on tickets?
faq.a: No. Agents work as usual. The hold only stops retention, deletion and erasure of the covered records.

glossary.definition: The tamper-evident record of sensitive actions in your workspace.
The way audit entries are linked, each with a fingerprint of the one before. A broken link shows that an entry was changed or removed.
A rule that archives, anonymises or deletes a kind of data after a number of days.
A count of what a retention policy would affect now, without changing anything.
A rule that preserves matching tickets and their records during a dispute, audit or investigation.
A customer's request to get a copy of their data or to have it erased.
To remove personal text from records but keep the numbers for reports.
Time-limited, read-only diagnostic access that you can grant to SupportDesk staff.
